claims.statement: HO-3 2011-05 governs policies written on or after 2011-05-01 that were written before the 2018 edition and continues to govern adjustment of losses under those policies regardless of report date; HO-3 2018-09 governs policies written on or after 2018-09-01, so 2018-only conditions cannot be imported into a 2011 policy.

Under HO-3 2011-05, Section I S.1 requires prompt notice to the insurer or agent and protection from further damage, S.2 requires a signed sworn proof of loss within 60 days after insurer request, S.3 requires full compliance and suit within two years after loss, and S.4 applies the Declarations deductible to each Section I loss.

Under HO-3 2018-09, S.1 retains prompt notice and protection duties and adds an inventory of damaged personal property; S.2 retains the request-triggered 60-day sworn-proof requirement; and S.4 keeps the full-compliance and two-year action limitation.

The HO-3 2018-09 base-form payment provision is S.3: payment is due 60 days after receipt of proof of loss and written agreement, an appraisal award, or a court judgment, while 2011-05 S.1-S.4 contains no corresponding payment provision.
Both HO-3 editions exclude loss caused by neglect, defined as failure to use all reasonable means to save and preserve property at and after loss, reinforcing their S.1 property-protection duties.

HO-3 2018-09 S.5 applies the Declarations deductible to each Section I loss, recognizes a separate state-required windstorm or hail deductible, and directs that only the larger is deducted where both apply.

For loss covered under a verified attached HO 04 90 endorsement, W.3 modifies rather than stacks with the selected base Section I Declarations deductible: 2010-10 applies a separate $500 deductible to each endorsement loss and 2026-01 applies a separate $1,000 deductible.

For a Texas HO 01 45 endorsement effective on or after 2022-01-01, T.1 implements Bulletin B-2021-08 by applying a separate windstorm/hail deductible expressed as a Coverage A percentage generally limited to 1%-5%, with a 10% seacoast maximum; the bulletin also permits a flat-dollar alternative no lower than the all-other-perils deductible.

Texas HO 01 45 and Bulletin B-2021-08 prohibit applying both the windstorm/hail and all-other-perils deductibles to the same wind/hail loss; for a mixed-peril occurrence, each deductible applies only to separately determinable damage, otherwise only the larger single deductible applies, and an unnotified renewal increase is ineffective for that term.

For an applicable Texas HO 01 45, T.4 extends the identified S.4 action period to two years and one day after loss, while T.5 separately requires acknowledgement within 15 days, written approval or denial within 15 business days after all reasonably requested items, and payment within five business days after approval notice; the T.4 S.4 cross-reference matches 2018-09's action section but not 2011-05's.

A Texas per-named-storm deductible period starts when the National Hurricane Center names the storm and ends 72 hours after designation is discontinued, with all wind/hail loss in that period treated as one occurrence; where wind/hail is excluded for Texas Windstorm Insurance Association coverage using the specified exclusion process, HO 01 45 T.1 does not apply.

For Florida personal residential policies issued or renewed on or after 2023-07-01, a separate roof deductible requires an offer of a policy without it at a filed and approved rate plus written premium-difference disclosure; an ACV roof schedule cannot apply to a roof under 10 years old, and a hurricane and separate roof deductible cannot both be applied to the same loss, for which only the larger is deducted.

Both HO-3 editions make the Section I A.3 sewer/drain-backup and sump-event exception dependent on attached HO 04 90; once attachment is verified, the 2010-10 endorsement remains applicable to policies written under it, while 2026-01 replaces it for policies written on or after 2026-01-01, independently of the base HO-3 edition selection.
HO 04 90 W.2 sets a default within-limit policy-period sublimit of $5,000 in 2010-10 and $10,000 in 2026-01 unless the endorsement Declarations state a higher limit.

Both HO 04 90 editions deny coverage where the stated known, causative, unremedied maintenance failure is established under W.5; in 2026-01 only, W.6 additionally makes coverage for a residence with finished area below grade conditional on an installed and operable serving-sewer backflow-prevention device at the time of loss.

The water-loss guide is internal claims guidance rather than policy authority and must not be quoted to an insured or claimant; its source-first investigation instruction does not alter the selected endorsement's contractual terms.

The controlling HO-3 edition is selected by policy written date, with HO-3 2011-05 governing policies written from 2011-05-01 through 2018-08-31 and remaining controlling for losses under those policies even if reported later, while HO-3 2018-09 governs policies written on or after 2018-09-01.

HO-3 2011-05 Section I conditions require prompt notice and protection of property from further damage, but do not state a separate inventory duty in S.1; HO-3 2018-09 S.1 adds preparation of an inventory of damaged personal property.
Both HO-3 editions require a signed, sworn proof of loss within 60 days after the insurer requests it, so the request date starts the proof-of-loss clock.

HO-3 2018-09 S.3 is the base-form loss-payment provision in these sources: the insurer adjusts losses with the insured and pays the insured unless another payee is named, and payment is due 60 days after receipt of proof of loss and written agreement, an appraisal award, or a court judgment.
HO-3 2011-05 does not contain the same base-form loss-payment clause in its Section I conditions; its Section I conditions stop at the deductible provision.

HO-3 2011-05 S.4 applies the deductible shown in the Declarations to each Section I loss, while HO-3 2018-09 S.5 applies the Declarations deductible and, where a separate windstorm or hail deductible required by a state amendatory endorsement also applies, deducts only the larger.

In both HO-3 editions, A.3 water-backup loss remains excluded unless HO 04 90 is attached; when attached, HO 04 90 provides the limited sewer/drain backup or sump overflow/discharge coverage, and the selected HO 04 90 edition must be verified independently of the HO-3 edition.

HO 04 90 W.3 is a contract deductible modification for covered endorsement loss, not a write-back of A.3, and it displaces the base Section I deductible; the deductible is $500 in edition 2010-10 and $1,000 in edition 2026-01.
HO 04 90 2026-01 adds a new W.6 backflow-prevention requirement for premises with a finished area below grade, and that requirement did not appear in edition 2010-10.

For a Texas policy with HO 01 45 attached and effective on or after 2022-01-01, T.1 amends HO-3 2018-09 S.5 and applies only the separate windstorm and hail deductible to windstorm or hail loss; the all-other-perils deductible is not also applied.

For a Texas mixed-peril occurrence under HO 01 45 T.1, if wind/hail damage and another covered peril can be separately determined, each deductible applies only to its respective portion; if the damage cannot be separately determined, only the larger single deductible applies to the entire loss.

Texas Bulletin B-2021-08 is regulatory authority that governs deductible disclosure, application, and filing requirements, but it does not by itself prove that HO 01 45 is attached to a particular policy.

HO 01 45 T.4 extends the action period to two years and one day after the date of loss, and T.5 separately requires acknowledgement within 15 days, written approval or denial within 15 business days after receiving reasonably requested items, and payment within five business days after approval notice.

HO 01 45 T.7 allows windstorm and hail to be excluded when the insured obtains that coverage through the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association, but only if the exclusion endorsement is attached and the insured's signed acknowledgment is obtained at binding; when that exclusion applies, T.1 does not apply.

Texas Bulletin B-2021-08 and HO 01 45 both permit a separate windstorm and hail deductible percentage of 1% to 5% of Coverage A, with a 10% ceiling in the seacoast territories defined by their respective sources; the bulletin also allows a flat-dollar deductible no lower than the all-other-perils deductible, while the endorsement text itself does not insert that flat-dollar option.

Texas Bulletin B-2021-08 requires separate windstorm and hail deductible disclosure on the declarations page in type no smaller than the all-other-perils deductible and requires 30 days' written notice before any increase in the deductible percentage becomes effective for a renewal term.
